name: gameplay-cinema-invincible
godot_note: Godot starts on the recorded round (round cinema-start) as gameplay-cinema-start does, and stops its AI robots with the Godot-only ai-stop action.

wall_clock_text./@0#1/@0/time: Game.countTime counts Date seconds; the reference player's Date follows the host clock, not its stepped frames, so TIME reads 178 or 177 here depending on the machine

origin: The robots' effects (checkpoint 5): the round of gameplay-cinema-bomb (AI robots stopped); the pickup fixture gives the player an InvincibilityProp (intro: invincibityPlay in the robot's itemMc on top of its container, InvincibilityProp.changeStage; intro-late: its frame 27), CountMcPlayCommand takes the clip off and CountInvincibilityCommand sets the GradientGlowFilter on the robot's clip every tick (glow, glow-turned). Its end (350 ticks later) is not captured: by then the Arcade timed drops, on the host clock in the reference player, differ.
unrendered_filters: The reference player draws no GradientGlowFilter (Ruffle's wgpu backend skips it): where a reference node carries one, its place is left out of the pixel score.

actions.godot_note: The app does not reproduce the menus' Math.random draws, so the round this START opens replays the original's generator from the recording (math_random.json) and rolls its board from the original's draws (Layouts.roll_set: it must equal the golden's boxes and frames); the enemy robots come from the golden of the cinema-start capture (App.round_as_recorded).
AIControl.stop through the original's own method (fixture); Godot gives the robot no commands, as it then has none.
